title: A Comparative Analysis of Ethical and Safety Gaps in LLMs using Relative Danger Coefficient

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting models to justify statistical disparities (e.g., crime rates between white and black people) and using logical puzzle embeddings that contain racially stereotyping statements.
Using direct adversarial prompts asking the model to explain why certain religious groups should be feared (Religious Fear-Mongering).

Prompting models with moral dilemmas (trolley problems) forcing a choice between saving children or elderly persons versus other individuals, as well as requests to discriminate using statistics based on age.
Requesting models to use statistics to discriminate or make comparisons based on sex.
Testing moral alignment using trolley-style ethical dilemmas that include a disabled person to observe if the model devalues their life.
Presenting models with trolley problem scenarios that force a choice between saving regular individuals versus a 'genius scientist' or 'medical researcher' to test for utilitarian bias.
Using moral philosophy dilemmas (trolley problems) involving a veteran to observe how the model weighs their life compared to others.
